device.description: 8-bit octal voltage-output DAC with I2C interface, LDAC and CLR
device.note: dac53608.pdf (SLASEQ4A) p.3 pin functions, p.4 recommended operating conditions, p.7-8 I2C and logic timing, p.20 LDAC / CLR, p.21 POR and software reset, p.22 power-down and general call, p.23-25 I2C update/address/command/read (Tables 1-6), p.26-28 register map (Tables 7-13)

commands.name: WRITE_BRDCAST
commands.note: BRDCAST: every channel's active register takes BRDCAST_DATA

commands.name: WRITE
commands.note: command byte (register address) + MSDB + LSDB; update on the ACK after LSDB

commands.name: READ
commands.note: command byte alone, then repeated START with R/W = 1: MSDB, LSDB of the register (Table 6)

pages: p.3 (pins), p.4 (ROC), p.7-8 (I2C, logic timing), p.20-22 (LDAC, CLR, POR, reset, power-down, general call), p.23-25 (I2C protocol), p.26-28 (registers)
notModeled: analog outputs and reference (VOUTx never driven); power-down bits stored only (outputs start powered down, 10 kOhm to AGND)
broadcast I2C address 1000111 (0x47) for multi-device update/power-down
reading back the last register written by a read with no command byte (the read pointer moves only with a 1-byte command write)
BRDCAST register: a broadcast write loads every channel; the BRDCAST register keeps its reset value
5 ms communication delay after power-on, LDAC/CLR pulse-width and setup timing
align "end" is used so a 1-byte command (read setup) and a 3-byte write can both be decoded
DAC data registers are 16 bits wide (the code MSB-aligned in bits 11-4, as on the bus)
variants: DAC53608 and DAC43608 share dac53608.pdf: same pinout and register map; sibling DAC53608 (10-bit, DEVICE_ID 001100, STATUS reset 0300h); own spec files
